approachQuestion.prompt:
Repair a nearly ordered log

An array is guaranteed to be a permutation of distinct integers and each value is at most k positions away from its final sorted position. Return the sorted values. 1≤n≤200000; 0≤k<n. Examples: [2,1,4,3,6,5], k=1→[1,2,3,4,5,6]; [3,1,2], k=2→[1,2,3].

Do not modify either input. Values are opaque comparison keys; hashing, radix, counting and bucket methods are outside the stated model. Choose the most efficient valid method that returns the required result for every allowed input.
constraints: Inputs are read-only and must remain unchanged.
Only comparison-based ordering is allowed; hashing, radix, counting and bucket methods are outside this problem model.
The k-displacement guarantee is with respect to ascending order and zero-based positions.

options.text: Keep the next at most k+1 values in a min-heap, repeatedly emit the minimum and insert the next unseen value.
options.feedback: The next global minimum must occur within the next k+1 positions.

options.text: Sort the entire array with comparison merge sort.
options.feedback: Always correct but ignores the promised bound on displacement.

options.text: Scan once from left to right and swap each adjacent inversion when first encountered.
options.feedback: One left-to-right pass transforms [2,3,1] into [2,1,3], still unsorted.

options.text: Reverse the first k+1 values and leave the rest unchanged.
options.feedback: The promise bounds displacement but does not imply reversal.

feedback.reason: The next correct output is among the next k+1 unseen candidates because displacement is bounded by k.
details: Initialize a min-heap with up to k+1 values; repeatedly remove its minimum and insert the next unseen value.
The next correct output is among the next k+1 unseen candidates because displacement is bounded by k. A heap of that frontier suffices; a heap of the full input discards the space benefit.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the fixed min-heap method revealed below, choose tight worst-case time and auxiliary-space bounds. Heapify at most k+1 values and then process all n entries using heap insert/remove; count heap storage and exclude input and returned output. Heap operations use a binary heap, comparisons are constant-time, and the output is preallocated.

options.text: O(n log(k+2)) time, O(k+1) auxiliary space
O(n log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space
O(n log(k+2)) time, O(n) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Maintain only the k+1-candidate frontier with logarithmic heap repairs.
details: The next output comes from a heap of at most k+1 candidates. Each of n emissions performs bounded logarithmic repairs, giving O(n log(k+2)); +2 covers k=0. Helper storage is O(k+1), not O(n) when k is small. Full sorting loses the displacement-sensitive bound, while linear-time repair is not guaranteed for a growing heap.
